blocks.h2: What to Do if a Pipe Bursts

steps.body: Find the main water valve, usually in the basement near the meter, and turn it clockwise.

steps.h3: 2. Turn Off Power Near the Water
steps.body: If water is near outlets or appliances, shut off the breaker for that area if you can do it safely.
This drains pressure from the lines and helps remaining water get out.

blocks.intro: It's not always a dramatic spray:

bullets: Water is escaping before it reaches the faucet.
With nothing on, you hear water moving in a wall or ceiling.

tiles.h3: A Wet Spot or Stain That Grows
bullets: On a ceiling, wall or floor, often near an outside wall.
Everything is off and the meter is still moving.

tiles.body: When it's below zero outside and one tap gives nothing, that line is likely frozen.
Visible frost on a pipe in a crawl space, garage or basement rim joist.
A blocked line can push odors back up.

blocks.h2: Why Pipes Freeze in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: Cook County winters bring stretches of below-zero nights. Homes here have a few common weak spots.

items.body: Kitchen sinks on outside walls are a classic freeze point, especially in older homes with little insulation in the wall.
Pipes running along the top of the basement wall or through a crawl space sit right next to cold air.
Many 1970s and 1980s homes have living space over an attached garage, with pipes running through the cold floor.
A hose left connected traps water in the spigot. Older spigots aren't freeze-resistant, and they split inside the wall.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: How do I thaw a frozen pipe safely?
items.preview: Open the faucet and warm the pipe slowly with a hair dryer or space heater. Never use an open flame.
items.answer: Open the faucet so water can flow once it thaws. Warm the pipe slowly with a hair dryer, a heating pad or a space heater, starting near the faucet. Never use a torch or open flame. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: How can I keep my pipes from freezing?
items.preview: Keep heat on, open cabinet doors on outside walls and drip faucets in a deep freeze.
items.answer: Keep the heat at 55 degrees or higher, even when you're away. Open the cabinet doors under sinks on outside walls, let faucets drip during very cold nights and disconnect garden hoses in the fall.

items.q: Why did my pipe leak days after the cold snap?
items.preview: It split while frozen and only leaked once it thawed.
items.answer: Ice expands and splits the pipe while it's frozen. The water only escapes once it thaws, which is why leaks often show up a day or two after the cold breaks.

items.q: Can you replace my outdoor spigot with a freeze-resistant one?
items.preview: Yes. It's one of the best ways to prevent a burst pipe.
items.answer: Yes. A freeze-resistant spigot shuts the water off inside the warm part of the wall. It's a small job that prevents a common burst pipe.
